title: Kernel scoring decay after scheduler heuristic deploy — remediation plan
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Summary: A scheduled heuristic adjustment to the scheduler's short-sequence bias caused sustained degradation in kernel scoring for fused-attention kernels across a subset of mid-length workloads. Symptoms first appeared as rising p95/p99 latency and throughput regression on several Hosted and Dedicated routes; impacted customers observed increased token cost and timeouts for long-running streams. This ticket tracks the follow-up work: root-cause remediation, short-term mitigations, telemetry improvements, and rollout guardrails.
incident_summary: 2026-03-01 09:14 UTC: Alerts triggered for elevated p99 generation latency on model rwd-gpt-7b / hosted-us-east. By 09:40, support confirmed multiple customer reports (Acme Chat, FinSec Corp) with timeouts and degraded UX. Investigation revealed scheduler heuristic 'short_seq_bias_v2' deployed 2026-02-28 increased weight for short-preferring kernels. Between 09:50–11:30 we saw progressive decay in kernel_score_normalizer values for fused-attn kernels; scheduler started routing more traffic to CPU-fallback and older quantized kernels causing 2–4x token latency increase for affected requests. Mitigation (10:45) rolled back heuristic and injected a temporary circuit-breaker that pinned kernel selection for hot models. By 12:05 latency returned to baseline. Postmortem initiated.
root_cause: The short_seq_bias_v2 change added an aggressive decay term in the kernel_score normalizer to favor kernels that showed shorter completion times. In mixed workloads the scheduler's short-probing traffic (synthetic warmup and client microbursts) biased the decay estimator, causing fused-attention kernels to be undervalued. Two implementation gaps amplified the effect: 1) no separation between probe and production traffic in kernel scoring, 2) the normalizer window was too small for models with multimodal sequence length distributions. Result: deterministic misranking of kernels and sustained routing to higher-latency variants.
mitigation_summary: Short-term: rollback short_seq_bias_v2 (done), enable temporary kernel-pinning for top N high-traffic models in hosted region (done), increase alert sensitivity for kernel_score delta (done). Medium-term: implement probe isolation, smooth kernel_score updates, and add circuit-breaker that can fallback to model-pinned kernel. Long-term: canonicalize kernel scoring semantics, add synthetic mixed-length canaries, and automate heuristic canary gating in console.
action_items: A1: Add 'probe' flag to scheduler traffic tagging so kernel scoring ignores synthetic probes — owner: Marco Rivera — due: 2026-03-10 (in progress)
A2: Increase kernel_score_normalizer window from 30s to 5m with exponential smoothing fallback — owner: Priya Nair — due: 2026-03-16
A3: Implement kernel_score_histogram and short_seq_ratio metrics in telemetry dashboard — owner: Linh Tran — due: 2026-03-12 (done)
A4: Add canary workload pipeline with mixed-length synthetic traces and automated failure gating in CI/console — owner: DevOps Team (lead: Omar Malik) — due: 2026-04-01
A5: Create runtime rollouts policy: any heuristic touching kernel scoring requires staged rollout with 72h mixed-canary and automated rollback — owner: Runtime PM (Nina Patel) — due: 2026-03-18
A6: Add a kernel-pinning API exposed via Console to allow emergency pin/freeze per-model — owner: Console Eng (Hannah Lee) — due: 2026-03-22
A7: Postmortem doc and external customer communication draft — owner: Sofia Chen — due: 2026-03-06 (done)
repro_steps: 1) Deploy short_seq_bias_v2 locally to runtime branch.
2) Run mixed-length synthetic generator with sequence lengths sampled: 10% < 8 tokens, 60% between 64-256 tokens, 30% > 1024 tokens.
3) Include warmup probe jobs that submit 5 short sequences every 30s (mimics global probe).
4) Observe kernel_score_normalizer decay for fused-attn kernels via /metrics/kernel_score_histogram and watch scheduler route share change.
5) Validate latency regression by running concurrent generation harness and compare token-p95/p99 against baseline.
Notes: reproducible in a 4-GPU dev pool with realistic concurrency (50 req/s).
telemetry_changes: Add kernel_score_histogram per-kernel and per-model (new metric: runtime.kernel_score.hist)
Add short_seq_ratio (runtime.request.len.short / runtime.request.len.total) and expose in per-route dashboards
Alert: kernel_score_delta > 0.25 sustained for >5m triggers P0 alert
Add labeled 'probe' boolean on scheduler traffic and exclude from scoring aggregation
